newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia king denies recognition to Ung Huot as PM.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king denies recognition to Ung Huot as PM.

text.p: Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk said on Monday he would not recognise the nomination of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as First Prime Minister, saying the position belonged to his ousted son Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

"While maintaining my affection for him, I will abstain from giving His Excellency Mr Ung Huot his new title of 'first prime minister'," Sihanouk said in comments released to news agencies in Beijing.
Ranariddh had the right to retain the title of first prime minister unless he was formally condemned by an independent Khmer tribunal, the king said.

The head of Cambodia's National Assembly on Monday called for Ung Huot to be approved as first prime minister in place of Ranariddh, who was overthrown by his rival premier Hun Sen in a bloody coup on July 6.
Parliamentary president Chea Sim made the call despite a weekend announcement by Ranariddh that Ung Huot was being temporarily expelled from his royalist FUNCINPEC party.

Ranariddh arrived in Beijing on Friday for what officials insist is a private visit with his father, who maintains a palatial residence in the Chinese capital where he has been undergoing medical treatment for several months.
Hun Sen has rejected calls from the king to travel to China for reconciliation talks with his ousted rival.
In his faxed comments, Sihanouk said he was still too ill to return to his troubled Southeast Asian homeland.
But the king made clear he was taking a keen interest in the affairs of the nation over which he reigns but does not rule.
The appointment of Ung Huot by an incomplete parliament would be invalid, Sihanouk said.

"The decisions of an incomplete parliament working under conditions of very questionable 'freedom' and 'regularity' could not be considered valid within the spirit of our 1993 Constitution and our liberal democracy," he said.
In an apparent recognition of Hun Sen's political grip on Cambodia, Sihanouk stressed he would not oppose laws passed since the second prime minister seized control.
As a constitutional monarch, he was obliged to let parliament chief Chea Sim choose which laws to sign into effect, Sihanouk said.
Hun Sen would be able to exercise full authority in Cambodia, he said, but did not elaborate.
Troops loyal to FUNCINPEC and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party have clashed sporadically since the coup.
But regional neighbours and Western powers have remained publicly optimistic about the chances of a political solution to the crisis.
Hun Sen's nomination of Ung Huot as first prime minister was seen by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) as credible, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Monday.
"It's...a credible form in parliament, certainly," Alatas, an ASEAN mediator in the Cambodian conflict, told reporters in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

"There were 97 members of parliament in all, and I think the quorum was only supposed to be 84 to 86," Alatas said, although he added it was unclear what the situation would be when the selection was confirmed.
Cambodian assembly officials said administrative delays meant voting could be held only in a week's time.
